存在 \(\gamma>0\)，仅依赖于 \(n,c_0,C_0\)，使下述结论成立。假定 \(0<h\le1\)，且三角多项式 \(f\) 的各频率 \(c_0/h\le|\xi|\le C_0/h\) 均位于一个球冠内，在一个标准正交标架中满足 \(\xi=(\xi',\xi_b)\)、\(\kappa=(\xi_b+|\xi|)/\sqrt 2>0\) 和 \(|\xi'/\kappa|\le\gamma\)。则
\[
 \|U(T)f\|_{L^{p_c}([1,2]\times\mathbb T^n)}
 \le C[\log(2/h)]^{2/p_c}\|f\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb T^n)}.
\]
常数 \(C\) 仅依赖于 \(n,c_0,C_0\)。
prop-6-3.title: 固定环面上频率球冠的临界估计

prop-6-3-proof.text:
零多项式的情形立即成立。对非零数据，归一化为 \(\|f\|_2=1\)，并针对给定环带固定孔径 \(\gamma\) 及常数 \(K\)，见 \ref{ms:prop-5-1}。先设 \(h<1/(8K)\)。令 \(a=Kh\)、\(b=2a\)，用 \(E(T,\tau)=\mathcal F(T,\tau)\) 表示命题~\ref{ms:prop-5-1} 的能量。该命题给出能量在开环域 \(a<|\tau|<4\) 上的非负性与光滑性，该环域包含闭环域 \(b\le|\tau|\le3\)。它还给出 \(\Delta_{T,\tau}E\le V(|\tau|)E\) 在 \(b<|\tau|<3\) 上成立，其中
\(V(s)=Cs^{-2}e^{-cs/h}\)。
对于 \ref{ms:lemma-6-1}，所需积分一致有界，因为
\[
 \int_b^3s\log(s/b)V(s)\,ds
 \le C\int_1^\infty \frac{\log t}{t}\,e^{-2cKt}\,dt .
\]
另有 \(V\) 在 \([1/2,3/2]\) 上一致有界。\ref{ms:prop-5-1} 在两个圆周上的界各自在整条圆周上一致。因而 圆周平均 \(H\)（对 \(E\) 取平均） 满足
\[
 H(0,2b)\le Ca^2\|f\|_{p_c}^{p_c},\qquad
 H(T,b)\ge ca^2\|U(T)f\|_{p_c}^{p_c}\quad(1\le T\le2).
\]
用 \ref{ms:lemma-6-1}，取 \(r=2b\)，约去 \(a^2\)，并取 \(p_c\) 次方根。由于 \(K\) 固定且 \(\log(3/(2Kh))\lesssim\log(2/h)\)，得所述断言。
所得不等式是齐次的，可通过重新伸缩去掉归一化。当 \(h\ge1/(8K)\) 时，所有有贡献的频率都在固定的球 \(|\xi|\le8KC_0\) 内。由 Hölder 不等式，每个这种频率处的 Fourier 系数不超过 \(\|f\|_{p_c}\) 的常数倍，且 \(e^{-iT|\xi|}\) 的模为一。对所得有限个逐点上界求和，即得此范围内的估计。
prop-6-3-proof.title: 固定环面上频率球冠的临界估计

shell-unit-radius.text:
设 $n\ge2$、$2\le p<\infty$、$\sigma>\max\{0,(n-1)/2-n/p\}$ 和 $0<c<C<\infty$。对 $0<\delta\le1/8$ 和 $\psi\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$，令 $A_{\delta,r}$ 的 Fourier 符号为 $\psi((1-|\xi|/r)/\delta)$。若 $g$ 为 Schwartz 函数，且 Fourier 支撑包含于 $c\le|\xi|\le C$，则
\[
\left\|\sup_{1\le r\le2}|A_{\delta,r}g|\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}
\le C_{c,C,n,p,\sigma,\psi}\delta^{-\sigma}\|g\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)} .
\]
给定 $C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$ 的有界子集，当 $\psi$ 在其中变化时，系数可统一选取。
shell-unit-radius.title: 单位尺度半径上的薄壳极大估计

shell-unit-radius-proof.text:
令 $U(t)=e^{-it|D|}$。取标量 Fourier 变换 $\widehat\psi(t)=\int e^{-itu}\psi(u)\,du$，由反演得
\[
 A_{\delta,r}g(x)=\frac{\delta r}{2\pi}
 \int_{\mathbb R}e^{itr}\widehat\psi(\delta rt)U(t)g(x)\,dt.
\]
关于 $1\le r\le2$ 的上确界由 $C_M\delta\int(1+\delta|t|)^{-M}|U(t)g(x)|\,dt$ 控制。在 $R\le|t|\le2R$ 上，其中 $R\ge1$ 为二进尺度，对时间变量用 Hölder 不等式并结合 \ref{ms:lemma-10-3}，得到 $L_x^p$ 界，所估计的贡献来自
\[
 C_M\delta(1+\delta R)^{-M}R^{1-1/p}R^{1/p+\sigma}\|g\|_p.
\]
对 $M>1+\sigma$，和为 $O(\delta^{-\sigma}\|g\|_p)$，可在 $R=\delta^{-1}$ 处分割求和得到。$|t|\le1$ 的贡献为 $O(\delta\|g\|_p)$，这是由 \ref{ms:lemma-10-3} 中的短时估计得到的。
shell-unit-radius-proof.title: 单位尺度半径上的薄壳极大估计

stein-annular-square.text:
平方函数论证需要一个一致的 $L^p$ 界，来控制作为伸缩算子输入的一列光滑环带截断函数。

\begin{Proposition}[环带 Littlewood--Paley 界]\label{ext:stein-annular-square}
设 $n\ge1$、$1<p<\infty$，令 $q\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ 支撑于 $\{c\le|\xi|\le C\}$，其中 $0<c\le C<\infty$。采用
\[
 \widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-ix\cdot\xi}f(x)\,dx,\qquad
 \check q(x)=(2\pi)^{-n}\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{ix\cdot\xi}q(\xi)\,d\xi .
\]
对 $j\in\mathbb Z$，在 Schwartz 函数上定义 $P_j=q(2^{-j}D)$，公式为 $\widehat{P_j f}(\xi)=q(2^{-j}\xi)\widehat f(\xi)$。在 $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ 上使用卷积公式 $P_j f=2^{jn}\check q(2^j\cdot)*f$。则
\[
 \left\|\left(\sum_{k\in F}|P_{k+\ell} f|^2\right)^{1/2}\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}
 \le C_{n,p,q}\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}
\]
对每个有限 $F\subset\mathbb Z$、每个整数移位 $\ell$ 和每个 $f\in L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ 成立。该界也适用于全和。未经伸缩的核 $\check q$ 为 Schwartz 函数且积分为零，因为 $q(0)=0$。它及其一阶导数的衰减给出 \cite{r-32}, Theorem~6.1.2, (6.1.3) 中的核界，因此 (6.1.4), p.~421 适用。限制到指标 $F+\ell$ 仍保持该界。
\end{Proposition}

thm-1-1.text:
设 \(n\ge2\)、\(2\le p<\infty\)、\(I=[1,2]\) 和 \(s_+(p)=\max\{0,(n-1)/2-n/p\}\)。采用 Fourier 变换约定
\(\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-iX\cdot\xi}f(X)\,dX\)
及反演因子 \((2\pi)^{-n}\)，令 \(U(T)\) 和 \(J\) 分别为符号为 \(e^{-iT|\xi|}\) 和 \((1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}\) 的乘子。
对每个 \(\varepsilon>0\) 及每个复值 Schwartz 函数 \(f\)，
\[
 \|U(T)f\|_{L^p(I\times\mathbb R^n)}
 \le C_{n,p,\varepsilon}\|J^{s_+(p)+\varepsilon}f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}.
\]
当 \(p=2\) 时可取 \(\varepsilon=0\)。
thm-1-1.title: 欧氏空间的局部光滑化

thm-1-1-proof.text:
当 \(p=2\) 时，Plancherel 定理和 \(|I|=1\) 给出结论，此时 \(\varepsilon=0\)。设 \(2<p<\infty\) 且 \(s=s_+(p)+\varepsilon\)。令 \(g=J^s f\)。在频率空间中取一个光滑单位分解，由紧支撑的低频截断 \(\chi_0\) 与二进环带截断 \(\psi(2^{-j}\xi)\) 组成，其中 \(j\ge1\)，并使用同一个固定的光滑紧支撑环带符号 \(\psi\)。选取光滑紧支撑的环带符号 \(\widetilde\psi\)，使它在 \(\operatorname{supp}\psi\) 上等于一。
乘子
\[
 m_j(\xi)=2^{js}\widetilde\psi(2^{-j}\xi)(1+|\xi|^2)^{-s/2}
\]
具有一致可积的核。事实上，尺度变换后，
\(m_j(2^j\eta)=\widetilde\psi(\eta)(2^{-2j}+|\eta|^2)^{-s/2}\)
的支撑落在固定的且远离零点的紧集内，各阶导数一致有界。因此反复分部积分给出逆变换的一致 \(L^1\) 界。尺度 \(2^j\) 的高频波为 \(2^{-js}U(T)\psi(2^{-j}D)m_j(D)g\)。
其时空范数不超过
\[
 C\,2^{-j\varepsilon}(1+j)^{\beta(p)}\|g\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)},
 \qquad
 \beta(p)=\min\{(n-1)(1-2/p),2/p\},
\]
这里使用了 \ref{ms:annular-lp} 和 Young 不等式。这些界对 \(j\ge1\) 可求和。

对于低频波，其乘子
\(e^{-iT|\xi|}\chi_0(\xi)(1+|\xi|^2)^{-s/2}\)
一致满足 Mihlin 导数界，其中 \(T\in I\)：每个 \(|\xi|^{|\alpha|}|\partial_\xi^\alpha m(\xi)|\) 在 \(\xi\ne0\) 上都一致有界，直至 \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\) 阶。因此，命题~\ref{ext:mihlin-multiplier} 给出一致的空间 \(L^p\) 界。由于 \(|I|=1\)，此界也控制时空范数。将低频和高频的界相加，证得该估计。对 Schwartz 数据，频率分解在分布意义下收敛到 \(U(T)f\)，而由范数上界可求和可知，\(L^p\) 极限与这一分布相同。
thm-1-1-proof.title: 欧氏空间的局部光滑化

thm-1-2.text:
设 \(n\ge2\)、\(p_c=2n/(n-1)\)、\(I=[1,2]\) 和 \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\})\)。采用 Fourier 变换
\(\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-iX\cdot\xi}f(X)\,dX\)
以及反演因子 \((2\pi)^{-n}\)。令 \(U(T)\) 为符号为 \(e^{-iT|\xi|}\) 的 Fourier 乘子。对 \(N\ge2\)，令 \(P_N\) 为符号为 \(\varphi(\xi/N)\) 的 Fourier 乘子。于是对每个复值 Schwartz 函数 \(f\)，
\[
 \|U(T)P_N f\|_{L^{p_c}(I\times\mathbb R^n)}
 \le C_{n,\varphi}[\log(2+N)]^{2/p_c}\|f\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb R^n)}.
\]
thm-1-2.title: 临界环带估计

thm-1-2-proof.text:
记 \(h=N^{-1}\)，选择固定紧环带 \(c_0\le|\eta|\le C_0\)，使其包含 \(\varphi\) 的支撑。取有限的光滑分解 \(\varphi=\sum_\nu\varphi_\nu\)，从属于该环带上孔径如 \ref{ms:prop-6-3} 所示的各球冠。在环面 \(\mathbb R^n/(100\mathbb Z)^n\) 上，将 \ref{ms:prop-6-3} 用于 \(\varphi_\nu(hD)F\)。其 \(L^{p_c}\) 范数一致不超过 \(C_\nu\|F\|_{p_c}\)：其卷积核是 \(h^{-n}\check\varphi_\nu(\cdot/h)\) 的周期化，而后者的 \(L^1\) 范数至多为 \(\|\check\varphi_\nu\|_1\)。这里 \(\check\varphi_\nu\) 表示逆 Fourier 变换。环面在一个基本立方体上采用通常的 Lebesgue 体积测度，因此周期化核在频率 \((2\pi/100)\mathbb Z^n\) 处具有相同的乘子符号。对 \(\nu\) 求和得到
\[
 \|U(T)\varphi(hD)F\|_{L^{p_c}(I\times\mathbb T^n)}
 \le C[\log(2/h)]^{2/p_c}\|F\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb T^n)}.
\]

在 \(\mathbb R^n\) 上，卷积核为
\[
 K_h(T,X)=(2\pi h)^{-n}
   \int e^{i(X\cdot\eta-T|\eta|)/h}\varphi(\eta)\,d\eta .
\]
对 \(T\in I\) 和 \(|X|\ge3\)，相位 \(\Phi=X\cdot\eta-T|\eta|\) 满足 \(|\nabla_\eta\Phi|\ge |X|/3\)，且二阶及更高阶导数在环带上一致有界。使用 \(h\nabla_\eta\Phi\cdot\nabla_\eta/(i|\nabla_\eta\Phi|^2)\) 作分部积分。去掉 \(h\) 后，系数及其各阶导数在支撑上均为 \(O(|X|^{-1})\)。因此反复进行 \(M+n\) 次，其中 \(M\ge1\) 为整数，得到
\[
 |K_h(T,X)|\le C_M h^M(1+|X|)^{-M}
 \qquad (T\in I,\ |X|\ge3).
\]
将 \(\mathbb R^n\) 用单位立方体 \(Q\) 铺满，令 \(10Q\) 为边长十的同心立方体。对 \(X\in Q\) 和 \(Y\notin 10Q\)，有 \(|X-Y|\ge9/2\)。故每个立方体上的远处贡献都由同一个函数控制，即
\[
 C_M h^M\big((1+|\cdot|)^{-M}*|f|\big)(X).
\]
对 \(M>n\)，此函数的 \(L^{p_c}(I\times\mathbb R^n)\) 范数至多为 \(C_M h^M\|f\|_{p_c}\)，这是由 Young 不等式和 \(|I|=1\) 得出的。

对于近处贡献，令 \(f_Q=f\mathbf 1_{10Q}\)。将 \(Q\) 的中心平移到原点，再将 \(f_Q\) 以 \(100\) 为周期作周期化。周期输入的范数为 \(\|f\|_{L^{p_c}(10Q)}\)。周期输出采用 \(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}K_h(T,X+100k)\) 作为核。对 \(X\in Q\)、\(Y\in 10Q\) 和 \(k\ne0\)，自变量 \(X-Y+100k\) 的长度至少为 \(94.5|k|\)，因为对每个非零坐标 \(k_j\)，有 \(|X_j-Y_j+100k_j|\ge 94.5 |k_j|\)。由衰减界及 \(M>n\)，在 \(I\times Q\) 上周期输出和欧氏输出的逐点差值至多为 \(C_M h^M\|f_Q\|_1\)。\(10Q\) 的体积固定，因此由环面估计与 Hölder 不等式得到
\[
 \|U(T)P_Nf_Q\|_{L^{p_c}(I\times Q)}
 \le C[\log(2/h)]^{2/p_c}\|f\|_{L^{p_c}(10Q)}.
\]
取 \(p_c\) 次幂并对 \(Q\) 求和。立方体 \(10Q\) 的重叠次数有统一上界。再加上远处输出，由 \(\log(2/h)\) 与 \(\log(2+N)\) 可比即得结论。
thm-1-2-proof.title: 临界环带估计

thm-10-1.text:
设 $n\ge 2$、$1\le p\le\infty$，且 $f\in L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ 任意。对于 $r>0$，令 $B_r^\alpha$ 为作用在 $\mathbb R^n$ 上、符号为 $(1-|\xi|^2/r^2)_+^\alpha$ 的 Fourier 乘子，并令
\[
\delta(p)=\max\{0,n|1/p-1/2|-1/2\}.
\]
若 $\alpha>\delta(p)$，则
\[
\sup_{r>0}\|B_r^\alpha f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}
\le C_{n,p,\alpha}\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}.
\]
在对 $\alpha$ 的相同条件下，平均值收敛到 $f$，收敛发生于 $L^p$ 中、在 $r\to\infty$ 时成立，其中要求 $p<\infty$。若 $2\le p<\infty$ 且 $\alpha>\max\{0,(n-1)/2-n/p\}$，则还有
\[
\left\|\sup_{r>0}|B_r^\alpha f|\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}
\le C_{n,p,\alpha}\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)},
\]
且这些平均值几乎处处收敛到 $f$，此时 $r\to\infty$。上确界针对一个几乎处处关于 $r>0$ 连续的代表元取值。
thm-10-1.title: Bochner--Riesz 平均

thm-10-1-proof.text:
记 $s_+(p)=\max\{0,(n-1)/2-n/p\}$。对 $2\le p<\infty$，选取 $s_+(p)<\sigma<\alpha$。取 $\eta\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$，使 $\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\eta(2^jv)=1$ 对 $v>0$ 成立。将其应用于 $v=1-\rho$，其中 $0\le\rho<1$。对 $\delta=2^{-j}\le1/8$，$(1-\rho^2)_+^\alpha$ 对应的分块等于
\[
\delta^\alpha\psi_\delta((1-\rho)/\delta),\qquad
\psi_\delta(u)=\eta(u)u^\alpha(2-\delta u)^\alpha,
\]
此表达式在 $\eta$ 的支撑外定义为零。各剖面函数的光滑半范数一致有界。余项在 $\rho=1$ 附近为零，在原点附近等于 $(1-\rho^2)^\alpha$，因此其径向延拓是光滑紧支撑的。该余项的核具有一个可积的径向递减控制函数。因此余项伸缩的上确界逐点由 Hardy--Littlewood 极大函数的常数倍控制。对其余各项用 \ref{ms:lemma-10-2}。它们对应的极大函数的 $L^p$ 范数之和由下式控制
\[
C\sum_{j\ge3}2^{-j(\alpha-\sigma)}\|f\|_p.
\]
这就证明了 Schwartz 函数的极大估计。在这一范围内 $\delta(p)=s_+(p)$，故也得到固定半径的界。

每个固定的 $B_r^\alpha$ 在 Schwartz 函数上自伴，且共轭指数满足 $\delta(p)=\delta(p')$。对偶性给出 $1<p<2$ 的固定半径界。当 $p=1,\infty$ 时，假设为 $\alpha>(n-1)/2$。径向 Fourier 反演给出单位半径的核，它等于 $|x|^{-n/2-\alpha}J_{n/2+\alpha}(|x|)$ 的常数倍，其中 $J_\nu$ 是第一类 Bessel 函数。核在原点有界，在无穷远处为 $O(|x|^{-(n+1)/2-\alpha})$，故其各伸缩核 $r^nK(rx)$ 具有相同的 $L^1$ 范数。对有限 $p$ 用稠密性，对 $p=\infty$ 使用卷积，得到所述延拓。

对有紧 Fourier 支撑的 Schwartz 函数，当 $r\to\infty$ 时，符号连同各阶导数在支撑上收敛到常数一及其相应导数。因此这些平均在 Schwartz 拓扑中收敛。由稠密性及固定半径界，可得 $p<\infty$ 时的范数收敛。为证明几乎处处收敛和极大估计，选取这样的 $f_j$，满足 $\sum_j\|f-f_j\|_p<\infty$。Schwartz 函数上的极大估计表明 $\sum_j\sup_{r>0}|B_r^\alpha(f_{j+1}-f_j)|$ 几乎处处有限。在每个这样的点处，$B_r^\alpha f_j$ 关于 $r>0$ 一致收敛到 $r$ 的一个连续函数；对于每个固定的 $r$，它几乎处处与有界的 $L^p$ 延拓相符。由于连续性，对 $r$ 取的上确界可测，由 Fatou 引理得 $f$ 的极大估计。最后，$f_j(x)\to f(x)$ 几乎处处成立，利用 $r$ 中的一致逼近，即可将 $r\to\infty$ 时的收敛从 $f_j$ 推广到 $f$。
thm-10-1-proof.title: Bochner--Riesz 平均

thm-11-1.text:
设 $n\ge2$、$2\le p<\infty$，且
\[
\alpha>\max\left\{\frac12,n\left(\frac12-\frac1p\right)\right\}.
\]
对于 $r>0$，令 $B_r^\alpha$ 为符号为 $(1-|\xi|^2/r^2)_+^\alpha$ 的 Fourier 乘子。对 $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ 定义
\[
\mathcal G_\alpha f(x)
 =\left(\int_0^\infty |r\partial_r B_r^\alpha f(x)|^2\frac{dr}{r}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
则 $\|\mathcal G_\alpha f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}\le C_{n,p,\alpha}\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}$，并且 $\mathcal G_\alpha$ 可延拓到 $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$。
thm-11-1.title: Stein 平方函数

thm-11-1-proof.text:
当 $p=2$ 时，对符号求导并对空间变量应用 Plancherel 定理。在内层积分中换元至 $u=|\xi|^2/r^2$，得到
\[
\|\mathcal G_\alpha f\|_2^2=
2\alpha^2\int_0^1u(1-u)^{2\alpha-2}\,du\,\|f\|_2^2
=\frac{\alpha}{2\alpha-1}\|f\|_2^2.
\]
假设 $p>2$。令 $s_+(p)=\max\{0,(n-1)/2-n/p\}$，选取 $\varepsilon>0$ 使 $\sigma=s_+(p)+\varepsilon<\alpha-1/2$。在 $r=2^k s$ 上，其中 $1\le s\le2$，令 $\rho=2^{-k}|\xi|$ 并采用测度 $dr/r=ds/s$，它与 $ds$ 可比。$r\partial_r B_r^\alpha$ 的乘子在 $\rho>s$ 时为零，其余情形等于
\[
 m(s,\rho)=2\alpha \rho^2s^{-2\alpha}(s+\rho)^{\alpha-1}(s-\rho)^{\alpha-1}
 \qquad (\rho<s).
\]
这是由对局部可积的正部幂求导得到的。由于 $\alpha>0$，边界不出现 Dirac 项。

取光滑截断函数，使它在 $\rho=s$ 附近等于一，并支撑在满足 $|s-\rho|<1/2$ 的地方，其中 $s\in[1,2]$。在 $s$ 中插入一个光滑截断，使它在 $[1,2]$ 上等于一，支撑于 $(3/4,9/4)$。$(s-\rho)^{\alpha-1}$ 前的因子与截断函数相乘，得到光滑紧支撑振幅 $A(s,\rho)$，其中 $\rho$ 有统一正下界。对 $s-\rho>0$，用光滑二进分解 $\sum_j\eta(2^j(s-\rho))=1$（$\eta\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$）分解此边界项。由支撑范围可知只剩 $j\ge0$。在其支撑上有 $\delta=2^{-j}$ 和 $\varphi(u)=\eta(u)u^{\alpha-1}$，每项的符号为
\[
 \delta^{\alpha-1} A(s,\rho)\varphi((s-\rho)/\delta).
\]

对每个 $\delta$，令 $T_\delta^{(k)}$ 为 \ref{ms:lemma-11-2} 中的算子的空间伸缩，保持 $s\in[1,2]$ 不变。在固定紧环带上作至多 $N=n+3$ 次分部积分，变量为 $\xi$，可得未经伸缩的核 $K$ 及其一阶空间导数具有衰减 $C\delta^{-N}(1+|x|)^{-N}$，且关于 $s$ 一致。特别地，同一估计适用于它们的 $H=L^2([1,2],ds)$ 与 $H^n$ 范数。选择光滑环带投影 $P_k$，它们是同一个乘子的伸缩，该乘子在未伸缩的频率支撑上等于一。将 \ref{ms:lemma-11-3} 应用于输入 $P_kf$，使用 \ref{ms:lemma-11-2} 中的界，所估计的量为 $B_p$ 和 $B_2$。命题~\ref{ext:stein-annular-square} 给出所选光滑环带投影的输入平方函数范数上界 $C\|f\|_p$。合并半径的所有二进区间，薄壳贡献至多为
\[
 C\delta^{\alpha-1}
 \left(\delta^{1/2}+\delta+
 [1+\log(1/\delta)]^{1/2-1/p}\delta^{1/2-\sigma}\right)\|f\|_p.
\]
对所有 $j$ 求和收敛，因为 $\alpha-1/2-\sigma>0$。

远离边界的其余乘子光滑。其支撑包含于 $\rho\le2$，其中 $s\in[1,2]$，且它在原点二阶消失。用光滑环带截断在 $\rho\asymp2^\ell$（$\ell\le2$）处分解它。将每项除以 $2^{2\ell}$，再将 $\rho$ 伸缩到单位环带，所得符号任意固定阶导数均一致有界。因此，未伸缩的核及一阶导数满足 \ref{ms:lemma-11-3}，其中 $\delta=1$，且 $C_*$ 可统一选取。相同的核衰减与卷积估计给出一致的 $B_2$ 和 $B_p$。对每个 $\ell$，使用尺度 $2^{k+\ell}$ 处的投影应用该引理。命题~\ref{ext:stein-annular-square} 取移位 $\ell$ 时，给出输入平方函数范数关于 $\ell$ 一致的界。由 $\sum_{\ell\le2}2^{2\ell}<\infty$，所得各界可求和。

这些估计起初适用于有限个 $k$ 和有限个壳层项。对 Schwartz 函数 $f$，乘子积分对每个固定 $r$ 收敛到原积分，因为幂函数 $(s-\rho)^{\alpha-1}$ 局部可积且分解中的重叠次数有统一上界。先在平方积分中，再在 $x$ 中应用 Fatou 引理，即得到任意有限个半径区间上的界。由单调收敛得到完整估计。由稠密性，线性映射 $f\mapsto (r\partial_r B_r^\alpha f)_{r>0}$ 延拓为到 $L_x^p(L^2(dr/r))$ 的有界映射，其逐点 Hilbert 范数也因此得以延拓。
thm-11-1-proof.title: Stein 平方函数

thm-a-1.text:
设 $m\ge1$，令 $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^m$ 为满秩格，令 $V\subset\mathbb R^{2m}$ 为有界光滑域。记 $\Omega=(\mathbb R^m/\Lambda)\times V$。用 $x_{a0}$ 表示周期坐标，将 $V$ 的其余坐标分组为 $(x_{a1},x_{a2})_{a=1}^m$，放在 $\mathbf i,\mathbf j$ 槽中。令 $(e_0,e_1,e_2)=(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j)$ 和 $\partial_{a\alpha}=\partial/\partial x_{a\alpha}$。对实函数 $v$，三槽 Hessian 为
\[
H_{ab}(v)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^2e_\alpha\bar e_\beta\,\partial_{a\alpha}\partial_{b\beta}v .
\]
该行列式采用 Moore 行列式。设 $r\in C^\infty(\overline V)$ 为定义函数，在 $V$ 内为负，满足 $\mathrm dr\ne0$（在 $\partial V$ 上），并满足 $H(r)>0$（在 $\overline\Omega$ 上）。设 $B_0,g\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)$ 取实值且满足
\[
 H(B_0)\ge0,\qquad g>\det H(B_0)\quad\text{on }\overline\Omega .
\]
则以下问题有唯一光滑至边界的解
\[
 \det H(B_0+u)=g,\qquad H(B_0+u)>0,\qquad u|_{\partial\Omega}=0.
\]
存在常数 $b\ge b'>0$ 使得 $br\le u\le b'r$。对这种区域和数据的光滑有限维族，障碍函数的常数可在局部统一选取；在局部光滑地等同各区域后，解光滑依赖于参数，直至边界。

比较原理在采用同一三槽算子的子域上也成立。若两个光滑实势函数 $\psi_i$ 的 Hessian 直至边界都正定，且子域内满足 $\det H(\psi_1)\ge\det H(\psi_2)$，其边界上满足 $\psi_1\le\psi_2$，则全子域上有 $\psi_1\le\psi_2$。
thm-a-1.title: 周期 Dirichlet 问题

thm-a-1-proof.text:
先在带边界的紧商空间 $\widetilde\Omega=\Omega\times(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^m$ 上工作，将数据沿新增的周期方向作常值延拓。在四槽基 $(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j,\mathbf k)$ 中，采用指标 $0,1,2,3$，原周期方向 $\Lambda$ 位于第 $0$ 槽，新周期方向 $\mathbb Z^m$ 位于第 $3$ 槽。重组实坐标，可将 $\widetilde\Omega$ 等同于环面 $\mathbb R^{2m}/(\Lambda\times\mathbb Z^m)$（第 $0,3$ 槽）与 $V$（第 $1,2$ 槽）的乘积。在降回原空间之前，$G,H$ 均表示完整的四槽梯度与 Hessian。记 $\mathcal H(D^2\psi)=H(\psi)$，并用 $\widehat\xi$ 表示实余向量 $\xi$ 按四槽编码所得的四元数列向量。引理~\ref{ms:lemma-3-1} 给出 $\mathcal H(\xi\xi^{\mathsf t})=\widehat\xi\widehat\xi^*$、$\operatorname{tr}H(\psi)=\Delta\psi$ 及在四元数酉坐标变换下的协变性。

\emph{比较和延拓。} 从已知解 $u=r$ 出发，按以下路径连接到所求的密度
\[
 g_t=(1-t)\det H(B_0+r)+tg,\qquad 0\le t\le1.
\]
在解 $\psi=B_0+u$ 处，令 $Q=H(\psi)$ 与 $S=\operatorname{tr}Q^{-1}$。由引理~\ref{ms:lemma-3-2}，对数行列式的导数及其实主符号为
\[
 Lw=Q^{-1}:H(w),\qquad \sigma_L(\xi)=\widehat\xi^*Q^{-1}\widehat\xi .
\]
因此 $L$ 在任一固定光滑解处一致椭圆，条件是在紧闭包上满足 $Q>0$。若两个势函数满足 $Q_i=H(\psi_i)>0$，对相应矩阵作插值得
\[
 \log\det Q_1-\log\det Q_2=
 \left(\int_0^1((1-\theta)Q_2+\theta Q_1)^{-1}\,\mathrm d\theta\right):H(\psi_1-\psi_2).
\]
当 Hessian 直至边界均正定时，平均后的实算子一致椭圆。由最大值原理得到四槽情形下的比较结论，并推出唯一性。同一论证适用于有界子域或带边界的紧商空间。

对每个 $k\ge0$ 和 $0<\alpha<1$，线性化 Dirichlet 算子 $L:C_0^{k+2,\alpha}\to C^{k,\alpha}$ 为同构，其中下标表示零边界迹。\cite{r-31}, Theorems 6.14 and 6.19 中的局部线性 Schauder 估计和 Dirichlet 理论适用于平直商空间的有限坐标覆盖。使用连续性方法，从 Laplace 算子变形到 $L$。在此过程中，定义函数 $r$ 始终是严格的障碍函数，因为 $H(r)\ge cI$。最大值原理给出此线性插值的一致 $C^0$ 估计，Schauder 估计给出相应的高阶界，且起始的 Dirichlet Laplace 算子可逆。现在对非线性方程应用隐函数定理，得到可解参数 $t$ 的集合为开集。

在此乘积空间上使用四槽 Hessian，引理~\ref{ms:dirichlet-c2} 为路径上的每个光滑解给出两个障碍函数以及一致的完整 $C^2$ 估计。

\emph{正则性、降回原空间与参数依赖。} $C^2$ 界和 $\det Q=g_t\ge c_0>0$ 给出 $cI\le Q\le CI$。因此实 Hessian 均位于紧凸集
\[
 \mathcal K=\{M:|M|\le C_1,\ cI\le\mathcal H(M)\le CI\}.
\]
上。在 $\mathcal H(M)>0$ 上，光滑函数 $F(M)=\log\det\mathcal H(M)$ 由引理~\ref{ms:lemma-3-2} 可知为凹函数。对 $M\in\mathcal K$，有
\[
 DF(M)[\xi\xi^{\mathsf t}]=
 \widehat\xi^*\mathcal H(M)^{-1}\widehat\xi
 \in[C^{-1}|\xi|^2,c^{-1}|\xi|^2].
\]
这些正是 $\mathcal K$ 上的实一致椭圆性与凹性假设，适用于 \cite{r-31}, Theorems 17.14 and $17.26'$ 的内部及边界估计，即 hypotheses (i)$'$ 和 (ii)$'$。为使算子定义在整个实矩阵空间上，将 $F$ 乘以一个光滑截断函数，令其支撑于满足 $\mathcal H(M)>0$ 的位置，且在 $\mathcal K$ 的一个邻域内等于一。估计所用的方程为 $F(D^2\psi)-\log g_t=0$，光滑边界值为 $B_0$。在有限坐标覆盖中应用这些局部估计，可得一致的 $C^{2,\alpha}$ 界，其中 $\alpha>0$ 取某个值。在可解参数的极限处，取一个在 $C^{2,\beta}$ 中收敛的子列，其中 $0<\beta<\alpha$。正定性与方程在极限下保持。通过 Schauder 估计逐步提高正则性，得到直至边界的光滑性：拉平边界后，利用给定的 Dirichlet 数据作切向求导，再由一致椭圆性从方程恢复纯法向二阶导数。这就证明了闭性，所以路径到达 $g$。

沿新增周期坐标的平移保持数据及区域不变。由 $\widetilde\Omega$ 上解的唯一性，解在所有这些平移下不变，因而可降到 $\Omega$。物理空间中的任意解都可提升，由此得到唯一性。通过同一提升也可得到物理子域上的比较原理。对于光滑族，将提升后的问题拉回固定域。其系数及边值光滑依赖于参数，且线性化算子与 Dirichlet 同构共轭。在每个 $C_0^{k+2,\alpha}$ 中应用隐函数定理，即得直到边界的光滑参数依赖。用于选取 $b,b'$ 的严格行列式不等式在该族中局部保持成立。
thm-a-1-proof.title: 周期 Dirichlet 问题

wave-cap-estimates.text:
设 $n\ge2$、$d=n-1$、$0<h\le1$ 和 $0<c_0<C_0$。取任意标准正交标架 $(x,b)$，位于 $\mathbb T^n=\mathbb R^n/(100\mathbb Z^n)$ 的覆盖空间上，在该标架中，记 $\xi=(\xi_x,\xi_b)$ 和 $\kappa=(\xi_b+|\xi|)/\sqrt2$。对满足 $\kappa>0$ 的频率，令 $v=\xi_x/\kappa$，并假设 $c_0\le h|\xi|\le C_0$ 与 $|v|\le1/10$。对 $y>0$ 和 $W\in\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}^d$，若 $|W|\le1/10$，其中 $\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}=\mathbb R+\mathbf k\mathbb R$ 和 $\mathbf k^2=-1$，令
\[
 b_0=\frac{1+\operatorname{Re}(W)\cdot v/2}{\sqrt2},\qquad
 \Psi=\kappa y|W-v|^2/2,\qquad
 m_0=b_0(\kappa/y)^{d/2}e^{-\Psi}.
\]
用 $\mathsf S_0$ 表示将 $\xi$ 处的系数乘以 $m_0$ 的乘子。在这些频率上，$\kappa\asymp h^{-1}$、$b_0\asymp1$，且
\[
 m_0^{-1}=b_0^{-1}(y/\kappa)^{d/2}e^\Psi
     \asymp(hy)^{d/2}e^\Psi .
\]
特别地，$h^d m_0\asymp1$ 在 $y\asymp h$ 时成立。

若 $f(X)=\sum_\xi c_\xi e^{\mathrm i X\cdot\xi}$ 为 $\mathbb T^n$ 上的三角多项式，且支撑于这些频率，则支撑内的频率数为 $O(h^{-n})$，且 $\sum_\xi|c_\xi|\lesssim h^{-n/2}\|f\|_2$。范数使用通常的环面体积。这些估计关于标架一致，常数依赖于 $n,c_0,C_0$；对于 $y\asymp h$ 时的双边估计，常数还依赖于 $y/h$ 的固定比较常数。
wave-cap-estimates.title: 环面频率球冠上的波乘子

wave-cap-estimates-proof.text:
命题~\ref{ms:prop-2-2} 表明 $m_0$ 是乘子的符号。因为 $|\xi|^2-\xi_b^2=|\xi_x|^2$ 且 $|\xi|+\xi_b=\sqrt2\kappa$，
\[
 |\xi|=\kappa(1+|v|^2/2)/\sqrt2 .
\]
环带界与 $|v|\le1/10$ 给出 $\kappa\asymp h^{-1}$。由界 $|\operatorname{Re}(W)\cdot v|\le1/100$ 得 $b_0\asymp1$。对 $m_0$ 取倒数，得到所述倒数公式。若 $y\asymp h$，则 $\Psi$ 有界，且 $(\kappa/y)^{d/2}\asymp h^{-d}$，由此得到双边估计。

在原始环面标架中，各频率属于 $(2\pi/100)\mathbb Z^n$。以原点为中心、半径 $C_0/h$ 的球包含该环带。以此球中的格点为中心取两两不交的格点立方体，边长为 $2\pi/100$，它们均落在半径 $C_0/h+\pi\sqrt n/100$ 的一个球内。由体积比较可知，立方体数不超过 $Ch^{-n}$，而旋转保持半径和体积。最后由 Parseval 恒等式得 $\sum_\xi|c_\xi|^2=100^{-n}\|f\|_2^2$，再由 Cauchy--Schwarz 不等式得系数的界。
wave-cap-estimates-proof.title: 环面频率球冠上的波乘子

wave-symbol.text:
设 $n\ge2$、$d=n-1$，取标准正交空间标架 $X=(x,b)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R$。令
\[
t=(T+b)/\sqrt2,\qquad s_0=(b-T)/\sqrt2,\qquad \mathsf X=(t,x,s_0).
\]
对于频率 $\xi=(\xi_x,\xi_b)$，若 $\xi_b+|\xi|>0$，令
\[
\kappa=(\xi_b+|\xi|)/\sqrt2,\qquad v=\xi_x/\kappa,\qquad
u_{\kappa,v}=c_{\kappa,v}\exp\!\left(\mathrm i\kappa(s_0+v\cdot x-|v|^2t/2)\right),
\]
其中 $\mathrm i$ 为 Fourier 变换中的通常虚单位。这就是物理相位为 $X\cdot\xi-T|\xi|$ 的平面波。令 $E_{ab}$ 为基本 $n\times n$ 矩阵，其指标为 $0\le a,b\le d$，令
\[
C^t=2E_{00},\qquad C^{x_j}=E_{0j}+E_{j0},\qquad C^{s_0}=-\sum_{j=1}^d E_{jj},
\qquad \mathcal P=\sum_\mu C^\mu\partial_{\mathsf X^\mu},
\]
再令 $C(p)=\sum_\mu p_\mu C^\mu$。给定 $p=\kappa(-|v|^2/2,v,1)$，
\[
-C(p)=\kappa
\begin{pmatrix}|v|^2&-v^{\mathsf t}\\-v&I_d\end{pmatrix},
\qquad -w^{\mathsf t}C(p)w=\kappa|w'-vw_0|^2\quad(w=(w_0,w')\in\mathbb R^n).
\]
核由 $E(v)=(1,v)^{\mathsf t}$ 张成，且整个向量波
\[
f_{\rm sys}=\sum_{\kappa,v}\kappa^{d/2}E(v)u_{\kappa,v}
\]
满足 $\mathcal P f_{\rm sys}=0$。这里在任意有限多个互异频率 $\xi$ 上求和，其中 $\xi_b+|\xi|>0$，以 $(\kappa,v)$ 对频率重新标记，系数 $c_{\kappa,v}\in\mathbb C$ 任取。对实状态 $w_1,w_2\in\mathbb R^n$，令 $z=w_1+\mathbf k w_2=(R,\zeta)\in\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}\times\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}^d$，其中 $\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}=\mathbb R+\mathbf k\mathbb R$ 和 $\mathbf k^2=-1$。位移
\[
q^\mu=\tfrac12\sum_{\ell=1}^2w_\ell^{\mathsf t}C^\mu w_\ell=\tfrac12z^*C^\mu z
\]
将每个在 $\mathsf X-\mathrm i q$ 处的模式乘以 $e^{p\cdot q}=\exp(-\kappa|\zeta-vR|^2/2)$。对每个固定的 $R$，$\kappa^{d/2}e^{p\cdot q}$ 的平方积分为 $\pi^d$，积分在 $\zeta\in\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}^d$ 上进行，其 $2d$ 个实坐标采用通常的 Lebesgue 测度。
wave-symbol.title: 零坐标、极化与 Gaussian 权重

wave-symbol-proof.text:
波算子在 $(t,x,s_0)$ 中为 $2\partial_t\partial_{s_0}+\Delta_x$，因此在频率 $\kappa$（$s_0$ 变量中）处变为 $2\mathrm i\kappa\partial_t+\Delta_x$。把 $T=(t-s_0)/\sqrt2$ 与 $b=(t+s_0)/\sqrt2$ 代入相位，因 $|\xi|^2-\xi_b^2=|\xi_x|^2$ 而得所述模式。$\mathcal P(\partial_{s_0}\psi,\nabla_x\psi)^{\mathsf t}$ 的第一分量为 $(2\partial_t\partial_{s_0}+\Delta_x)\psi$，其他分量因导数可交换而抵消。直接计算 $C(p)$ 得到所列分块矩阵。它的二次型为所述平方，核由 $E(v)$ 的倍数组成。作用在该模式上时，$\mathcal P$ 等同于乘以 $\mathrm i C(p)$，由此得到向量解。

在物理坐标中按 $-\mathrm i\rho(1,\omega)$ 平移，其中 $\rho>0$ 和 $|\omega|=1$，等同于将模式乘以 $e^{\rho(\xi\cdot\omega-|\xi|)}=e^{-\rho|\xi||\xi/|\xi|-\omega|^2/2}$。在 $|\xi|\asymp N$ 和 $\rho N\gg1$ 处，其角宽量级为 $(\rho N)^{-1/2}$。二次通量 $q(w)^\mu=w^{\mathsf t}C^\mu w/2$ 在零坐标标架中为 $(w_0^2,w_0w',-|w'|^2/2)$。在物理坐标中，其时间分量与空间部分的长度均等于 $(w_0^2+|w'|^2/2)/\sqrt2$。在 $w=E(v)$ 处，物理通量为 $(|\xi|,\xi)/\kappa$。

在两个通量之和中，由对称性可知 $z^*C^\mu z$ 的混合项抵消。对每个实状态使用 $-C(p)$ 的二次型，得到 $p\cdot q=-\kappa|\zeta-vR|^2/2$。将 $\kappa^d e^{-\kappa|\zeta-vR|^2}$ 的积分在 $2d$ 个实坐标中平移并伸缩，得到 $\pi^d$。
wave-symbol-proof.title: 零坐标、极化与 Gaussian 权重

levels.component_tex:
Let \(n\ge2\), \(p_c=2n/(n-1)\), \(I=[1,2]\), and
\(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\})\). Use the Fourier transform
\(\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-iX\cdot\xi}f(X)\,dX\), with
inverse factor \((2\pi)^{-n}\). Let \(U(T)\) be the Fourier multiplier
with symbol \(e^{-iT|\xi|}\). For \(N\ge2\), let \(P_N\) be the
Fourier multiplier with symbol \(\varphi(\xi/N)\). Then, for every
complex Schwartz function \(f\),
\[
 \|U(T)P_N f\|_{L^{p_c}(I\times\mathbb R^n)}
 \le C_{n,\varphi}[\log(2+N)]^{2/p_c}\|f\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb R^n)}.
\]

levels.component_tex:
Let \(n\ge2\), \(2\le p<\infty\), \(I=[1,2]\), and
\(s_+(p)=\max\{0,(n-1)/2-n/p\}\). With the Fourier convention
\(\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-iX\cdot\xi}f(X)\,dX\) and
inverse factor \((2\pi)^{-n}\), let \(U(T)\) and \(J\) be the
multipliers \(e^{-iT|\xi|}\) and \((1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}\), respectively.
For every \(\varepsilon>0\) and every complex Schwartz function \(f\),
\[
 \|U(T)f\|_{L^p(I\times\mathbb R^n)}
 \le C_{n,p,\varepsilon}\|J^{s_+(p)+\varepsilon}f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}.
\]
At \(p=2\) one can take \(\varepsilon=0\).

levels.title: Euclidean local smoothing

levels.component_tex:
Let \(n\ge2\), \(p_c=2n/(n-1)\), and let \(d\sigma\) be surface measure on \(S^{n-1}\). Write
\[
 Eg(X)=\int_{S^{n-1}} e^{iX\cdot\omega}g(\omega)\,d\sigma(\omega).
\]
Let \(T_\delta(\omega,x)\) be the open \(\delta\)-neighborhood of \(x+[-1/2,1/2]\omega\). Define \(K_\delta f(\omega)\) as the supremum over \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) of the average of \(|f|\) over \(T_\delta(\omega,x)\). For \(R\ge2\), \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(0<\delta\le1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|Eg\|_{L^{p_c}(B(z,R))}&\le C_n[\log(2+R)]^{2/p_c}\|g\|_{L^{p_c}(S^{n-1})},\\
 \|K_\delta f\|_{L^n(S^{n-1})}&\le C_n[\log(2/\delta)]^{4/p_c}\|f\|_{L^n(\mathbb R^n)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every subset of \(\mathbb R^n\) containing a unit line segment in each direction has Hausdorff dimension \(n\).

levels.title: Spherical extension and Kakeya

levels.component_tex:
Let \(n\ge2\), \(p_c=2n/(n-1)\), and write \(a'\) for the Hölder conjugate of \(a\). On \(S^{n-1}\) with surface measure \(d\sigma\), put \(Eg(x)=\int e^{ix\cdot\omega}g(\omega)\,d\sigma(\omega)\). On the truncated cone \(\Sigma=\{(\rho\omega,\rho):1\le\rho\le2,\ \omega\in S^{n-1}\}\) with induced surface measure \(d\Sigma\), put
\[
 E_\Sigma G(x,t)=\int_\Sigma e^{i(x\cdot\xi+t\tau)}G(\xi,\tau)\,d\Sigma(\xi,\tau).
\]
If \(1<a\le\infty\), \(b<\infty\), and \(b>p_c\) and \(b>(n+1)a'/(n-1)\), then the strong bounds
\[
 \|Eg\|_{L^b(\mathbb R^n)}\lesssim_{n,a,b}\|g\|_{L^a(S^{n-1})},\qquad
 \|E_\Sigma G\|_{L^b(\mathbb R^{n+1})}\lesssim_{n,a,b}\|G\|_{L^a(\Sigma)}
\]
hold. For \(b=\infty\) both bounds hold for every \(1\le a\le\infty\).

levels.title: Nikodym maximal estimate

levels.component_tex:
Let $n\ge 2$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and let $f\in L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ be arbitrary. For $r>0$ let $B_r^\alpha$ be the Fourier multiplier on $\mathbb R^n$ with symbol $(1-|\xi|^2/r^2)_+^\alpha$, and put
\[
\delta(p)=\max\{0,n|1/p-1/2|-1/2\}.
\]
If $\alpha>\delta(p)$, then
\[
\sup_{r>0}\|B_r^\alpha f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}
\le C_{n,p,\alpha}\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}.
\]
Under the same condition on $\alpha$, the means converge to $f$ in $L^p$ as $r\to\infty$ if $p<\infty$. If $2\le p<\infty$ and $\alpha>\max\{0,(n-1)/2-n/p\}$, then also
\[
\left\|\sup_{r>0}|B_r^\alpha f|\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}
\le C_{n,p,\alpha}\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)},
\]
and the means converge to $f$ almost everywhere as $r\to\infty$. The supremum is taken for a representative continuous in $r>0$ almost everywhere.

levels.title: Bochner--Riesz means

levels.component_tex:
Let $n\ge2$, $2\le p<\infty$, and
\[
\alpha>\max\left\{\frac12,n\left(\frac12-\frac1p\right)\right\}.
\]
For $r>0$ let $B_r^\alpha$ be the Fourier multiplier with symbol $(1-|\xi|^2/r^2)_+^\alpha$. For $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ define
\[
\mathcal G_\alpha f(x)
 =\left(\int_0^\infty |r\partial_r B_r^\alpha f(x)|^2\frac{dr}{r}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Then $\|\mathcal G_\alpha f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}\le C_{n,p,\alpha}\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}$, and $\mathcal G_\alpha$ extends to $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$.

levels.title: Stein's square function

levels.component_tex:
Let $d\geq 1$, $p_c=2(d+1)/d$, and $B_d=B(0,1)\subset\mathbb R^d$. For $g$ on $B_d$ set
\[
Eg(x,t)=\int_{B_d}e^{\mathrm i(x\cdot v+t|v|^2)}g(v)\,\mathrm dv.
\]
If $1<a\leq\infty$, $p_c<b<\infty$, and $b>(d+2)a'/d$, where $1/a+1/a'=1$, then
\[
\|Eg\|_{L^b(\mathbb R^{d+1})}\lesssim_{d,a,b}\|g\|_{L^a(B_d)}.
\]

Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be a compact interval, and let $S(t)=e^{\mathrm i t\Delta}$ denote the Fourier multiplier $e^{-\mathrm i t|\xi|^2}$ on $\mathbb R^d$. If $N\geq 2$ and $f$ is Schwartz with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat f\subset B(0,N)$, then
\[
\|S(t)f\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb R^d\times I)}
 \lesssim_{d,I}[\log(2+N)]^{2/p_c}\|f\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb R^d)}.
\]

If $p_c<p<\infty$ and $p\leq r\leq\infty$, set $s=d(1-2/p)-2/r$, with $1/\infty=0$. For every Schwartz $f$,
\[
\|S(t)f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d;L^r(I))}
 \lesssim_{d,p,r,I}\|f\|_{B^s_{p,p}(\mathbb R^d)}
 \lesssim_{d,p,s}\|(1-\Delta)^{s/2}f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}.
\]
Here $B^s_{p,p}$ is the inhomogeneous Besov space, defined using smooth inhomogeneous dyadic Fourier projections $P_j$ by the norm $(\sum_{j\geq 0}2^{jsp}\|P_jf\|_p^p)^{1/p}$. The cases $r=p$ and $r=\infty$ give, respectively, the spacetime estimate at order $d-2(d+1)/p$ and the maximal estimate at order $d(1-2/p)$.

levels.title: Paraboloid extension and Schr\"odinger local smoothing

levels.component_tex:
Fix \(n\ge2\) and \(0<c_0<C_0\), and put \(p_c=2n/(n-1)\).
Let \(\mathbb T^n=\mathbb R^n/(100\mathbb Z)^n\), with Lebesgue
volume on a fundamental cube. Define \(U(T)\) by its multiplier
\(e^{-iT|\xi|}\) on the torus frequencies \((2\pi/100)\mathbb Z^n\).
There is \(\gamma>0\), depending only on \(n,c_0,C_0\), such that
the following holds. Suppose \(0<h\le1\) and a trigonometric
polynomial \(f\) has frequencies \(c_0/h\le|\xi|\le C_0/h\) in
one cap, expressed in an orthonormal frame as
\(\xi=(\xi',\xi_b)\), \(\kappa=(\xi_b+|\xi|)/\sqrt 2>0\), and
\(|\xi'/\kappa|\le\gamma\). Then
\[
 \|U(T)f\|_{L^{p_c}([1,2]\times\mathbb T^n)}
 \le C[\log(2/h)]^{2/p_c}\|f\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb T^n)}.
\]
The constant \(C\) depends only on \(n,c_0,C_0\).

levels.title: Critical estimate on a fixed torus cap

levels.component_tex:
Write \(h=N^{-1}\) and choose a fixed compact annulus
\(c_0\le|\eta|\le C_0\) containing the support of \(\varphi\).
Choose a smooth finite partition \(\varphi=\sum_\nu\varphi_\nu\)
subordinate to caps of the aperture in \ref{ms:prop-6-3} for this
annulus. On the torus \(\mathbb R^n/(100\mathbb Z)^n\), apply
\ref{ms:prop-6-3} to \(\varphi_\nu(hD)F\). Its \(L^{p_c}\) norm is
bounded uniformly by \(C_\nu\|F\|_{p_c}\): its convolution kernel
is the periodization of \(h^{-n}\check\varphi_\nu(\cdot/h)\),
whose \(L^1\) norm is at most \(\|\check\varphi_\nu\|_1\).
Here \(\check\varphi_\nu\) denotes the inverse Fourier transform.
The torus carries ordinary Lebesgue volume on a fundamental cube,
so the periodized kernel has the same multiplier at frequencies
\((2\pi/100)\mathbb Z^n\). Summing over \(\nu\) yields
\[
 \|U(T)\varphi(hD)F\|_{L^{p_c}(I\times\mathbb T^n)}
 \le C[\log(2/h)]^{2/p_c}\|F\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb T^n)}.
\]

On \(\mathbb R^n\) the convolution kernel is
\[
 K_h(T,X)=(2\pi h)^{-n}
   \int e^{i(X\cdot\eta-T|\eta|)/h}\varphi(\eta)\,d\eta .
\]
For \(T\in I\) and \(|X|\ge3\), the phase \(\Phi=X\cdot\eta-T|\eta|\)
satisfies \(|\nabla_\eta\Phi|\ge |X|/3\), and its derivatives of
order at least two are uniformly bounded on the annulus. Integrate
by parts with \(h\nabla_\eta\Phi\cdot\nabla_\eta/(i|\nabla_\eta\Phi|^2)\).
The coefficient without \(h\) and all of its derivatives on the
support are \(O(|X|^{-1})\). Thus \(M+n\) iterations for integer
\(M\ge1\) give
\[
 |K_h(T,X)|\le C_M h^M(1+|X|)^{-M}
 \qquad (T\in I,\ |X|\ge3).
\]
Tile \(\mathbb R^n\) by unit cubes \(Q\), and let \(10Q\) be the
concentric cube of side ten. For \(X\in Q\) and \(Y\notin 10Q\)
one has \(|X-Y|\ge9/2\). On every cube the far contribution is
therefore bounded by the single function
\[
 C_M h^M\big((1+|\cdot|)^{-M}*|f|\big)(X).
\]
For \(M>n\), this function has \(L^{p_c}(I\times\mathbb R^n)\)
norm at most \(C_M h^M\|f\|_{p_c}\) by Young's inequality and
\(|I|=1\).

For the near contribution put \(f_Q=f\mathbf 1_{10Q}\). Translate the
center of \(Q\) to the origin and periodize \(f_Q\) at period \(100\).
The periodic input has norm \(\|f\|_{L^{p_c}(10Q)}\). The periodic
output uses \(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}K_h(T,X+100k)\) as its kernel.
For \(X\in Q\), \(Y\in 10Q\), and \(k\ne0\), the argument
\(X-Y+100k\) has length at least \(94.5|k|\): for every nonzero
coordinate \(k_j\), \(|X_j-Y_j+100k_j|\ge 94.5 |k_j|\).
The decay bound and \(M>n\) show that the periodic and Euclidean
outputs differ on \(I\times Q\) by at most
\(C_M h^M\|f_Q\|_1\) pointwise. The volume of \(10Q\) is fixed, so
the torus bound and Hölder's inequality give
\[
 \|U(T)P_Nf_Q\|_{L^{p_c}(I\times Q)}
 \le C[\log(2/h)]^{2/p_c}\|f\|_{L^{p_c}(10Q)}.
\]
Take \(p_c\)-th powers and sum over \(Q\). The cubes \(10Q\) have
bounded overlap. Adding the far output proves the result since
\(\log(2/h)\) is comparable to \(\log(2+N)\).

levels.title: Critical annular estimate

levels.component_tex:
Let $n\ge2$, $d=n-1$, $p_c=2n/d$, and fix $0<c_1<c_2$. On the spatial torus $\mathbb T^n=\mathbb R^n/(100\mathbb Z)^n$ write $X=(x,b)$ in an orthonormal frame with $x\in\mathbb R^d$. For each frequency with $\xi_b+|\xi|>0$ put $\kappa=(\xi_b+|\xi|)/\sqrt2$ and $v=\xi_x/\kappa$. There are constants $\gamma>0$, $K\ge1$, and $c,C>0$, depending only on $n,c_1,c_2$, with the following property. Let $0<h<1/(4K)$, $a=Kh$, and let $f$ be a trigonometric polynomial of $L^2$ norm one whose Fourier support consists of frequencies with $c_1\le h|\xi|\le c_2$, $\xi_b+|\xi|>0$, and $|v|\le\gamma$. Write $g_T=e^{-\mathrm i T|D|}f$.

Here is the energy used in the conclusion. For $z=(T,\tau)$, where $\tau$ lies in the quaternionic complex plane $\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}$ and $s=|\tau|\in(a,4)$, the auxiliary spatial coordinates are $(P,Z)\in\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}^{d}\times\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}$. Set
\[
Y=(\tau+Z)/\sqrt2,\quad S_1=(Z-\tau)/\sqrt2,\quad
y=|Y|,\quad W=P/Y,\quad \Phi=S_1+P\cdot P/(2Y),\quad Q=\Phi/a .
\]
Dots between complex vectors are bilinear. Take $w_0=1/10$ and let $\Omega_z$ be the torus times the auxiliary domain $Y\ne0$, $r=|W|^2/w_0^2+100|Q|^2-1<0$. Write $\mathrm d\zeta=\mathrm dX\,\mathrm dP\,\mathrm dZ$. The full quaternionic Hessian and gradient $H,G$ use the three real slots $(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j)$ for each index, where $\mathbf k\mathbf i=\mathbf j$. In these slots with basis $e_\alpha$, their entries are
\[
H_{ab}(w)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^2 e_\alpha\overline{e_\beta}\,\partial_{a\alpha}\partial_{b\beta}w,\qquad
G_a(w)=\sum_{\alpha=0}^2e_\alpha\partial_{a\alpha}w .
\]
A subscript $\mathrm{fib}$ takes the spatial block at fixed $z$. Determinants and cofactors of these Hermitian matrices are the Moore determinant and its matrix derivative, respectively.

For $\ell>0$ let $J_\ell$ be the periodization of $c_n\ell^{-n}(1+|X/\ell|^2)^{-n-2}$, with $c_n$ chosen so the kernel integrates to one. Let $0\le g\le1$ be a fixed smooth cutoff equal to one on $|Q|\le1/100$ and zero on $|Q|\ge1/20$. The wave current $A^0=\chi\chi^*$ in null coordinates is given by
\[
\chi=\sum_\xi
\begin{pmatrix}1\\(v+W)/2\\-W\cdot v/2\end{pmatrix}
\iota_{Y/y}(\overline{\widehat f(\xi)e^{\mathrm i(X\cdot\xi-T|\xi|)}})
(\kappa/y)^{d/2}e^{-\kappa y|W-v|^2/2},
\qquad
\iota_e(\alpha+\mathrm i\beta)=\alpha+e\mathbf i\beta .
\]
Return to physical coordinates by $T=(t-s_0)/\sqrt2$, $b=(t+s_0)/\sqrt2$ in the coordinate index. With convolution in $X$, put
\[
A_{\mathrm w}=g(Q)(J_h*A^0),\qquad
\mu=(A_{\mathrm w})_{TT}+h^{50n}\operatorname{Cof}(H(r))_{TT},\qquad
B_0=\lambda|\Phi|^2,\quad \lambda=h^{-30n},\quad
D_w=H_{\mathrm{fib}}(B_0+w).
\]
For the smooth zero-boundary solution $u$ of $D_u>0$, $\det D_u=\lambda\mu$ on the fiber, set
\[
\mathcal F(T,\tau)=\int_{\Omega_z}(-u)\mu\,\mathrm d\zeta+
\frac1\lambda\int_{\Omega_z}u\left(\int_0^1\det D_{\theta u}\,\mathrm d\theta\right)\mathrm d\zeta .
\]
The energy $\mathcal F$ is nonnegative and smooth on the open parameter domain $\mathbb R_T\times\{\tau:a<|\tau|<4\}$. With all norms on the torus,
\begin{align*}
\mathcal F(0,\tau)&\le Ca^2\|f\|_{p_c}^{p_c} && (|\tau|=4a),\\
\mathcal F(T,\tau)&\ge ca^2\|g_T\|_{p_c}^{p_c} && (|\tau|=2a),\\
\Delta_z\mathcal F(T,\tau)&\le Cs^{-2}e^{-cs/h}\mathcal F(T,\tau) && (2a\le s\le3).
\end{align*}
The last two estimates hold for all real $T$, and $\Delta_z$ is the Euclidean Laplacian in $T$ and the two real coordinates of $\tau$.

levels.title: Energy estimates on a fixed fiber

levels.component_tex:
Let \(M\ge0\), \(0<b<1/4\), \(D=\log(3/b)\), and let
\(V:[b,3]\to[0,\infty)\) be continuous with
\[
 \int_b^3 s\log(s/b)V(s)\,ds\le M,\qquad
 \sup_{1/2\le s\le3/2}V(s)\le M .
\]
Let \(E\ge0\) be smooth on
\(\mathbb R_T\times\{\tau\in\mathbb R^2:b\le|\tau|\le3\}\) and
assume \(\Delta_{T,\tau}E\le V(|\tau|)E\) in the interior.
Set
\[
 H(T,s)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}
    E(T,s(\cos\theta,\sin\theta))\,d\theta .
\]
There is a positive constant \(c(M)\) such that for \(b\le r\le1\),
\[
 H(0,r)\ge c(M)\frac{\log(r/b)}{D^2}\int_1^2H(T,b)\,dT .
\]

levels.title: Propagation across a thin cylinder

levels.component_tex:
The zero polynomial is immediate. For nonzero data, normalize
\(\|f\|_2=1\) and fix the aperture \(\gamma\) and the constant
\(K\) of \ref{ms:prop-5-1} for the given annulus. First assume
\(h<1/(8K)\). Put \(a=Kh\), \(b=2a\), and write
\(E(T,\tau)=\mathcal F(T,\tau)\) for the energy of Proposition~\ref{ms:prop-5-1}. This proposition supplies nonnegativity and smoothness on the open annulus \(a<|\tau|<4\), which contains the closed annulus \(b\le|\tau|\le3\). It also gives
\(\Delta_{T,\tau}E\le V(|\tau|)E\) on \(b<|\tau|<3\), with
\(V(s)=Cs^{-2}e^{-cs/h}\). For \ref{ms:lemma-6-1} the required
integral is uniformly bounded because
\[
 \int_b^3s\log(s/b)V(s)\,ds
 \le C\int_1^\infty \frac{\log t}{t}\,e^{-2cKt}\,dt .
\]
Also \(V\) is uniformly bounded on \([1/2,3/2]\). The bounds of
\ref{ms:prop-5-1} at the two circles hold uniformly on each
circle. Thus the circular mean \(H\) of \(E\) satisfies
\[
 H(0,2b)\le Ca^2\|f\|_{p_c}^{p_c},\qquad
 H(T,b)\ge ca^2\|U(T)f\|_{p_c}^{p_c}\quad(1\le T\le2).
\]
Use \ref{ms:lemma-6-1} at \(r=2b\), cancel \(a^2\), and take
\(p_c\)-th roots. This gives the claim because \(K\) is fixed and
\(\log(3/(2Kh))\lesssim\log(2/h)\).
The resulting inequality is homogeneous, so the normalization is
removed by rescaling. When \(h\ge1/(8K)\) all contributing

levels.section_title: Critical estimate on a fixed torus cap: Proof of Proposition prop-6-3
levels.statement:
Fix \(n\ge2\) and \(0<c_0<C_0\), and put \(p_c=2n/(n-1)\).
Let \(\mathbb T^n=\mathbb R^n/(100\mathbb Z)^n\), with Lebesgue
volume on a fundamental cube. Define \(U(T)\) by its multiplier
\(e^{-iT|\xi|}\) on the torus frequencies \((2\pi/100)\mathbb Z^n\).
There is \(\gamma>0\), depending only on \(n,c_0,C_0\), such that
the following holds. Suppose \(0<h\le1\) and a trigonometric
polynomial \(f\) has frequencies \(c_0/h\le|\xi|\le C_0/h\) in
one cap, expressed in an orthonormal frame as
\(\xi=(\xi',\xi_b)\), \(\kappa=(\xi_b+|\xi|)/\sqrt 2>0\), and
\(|\xi'/\kappa|\le\gamma\). Then
\[

 \le C[\log(2/h)]^{2/p_c}\|f\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb T^n)}.
\]
The constant \(C\) depends only on \(n,c_0,C_0\).
levels.text:
The zero polynomial is immediate. For nonzero data, normalize
\(\|f\|_2=1\) and fix the aperture \(\gamma\) and the constant
\(K\) of \ref{ms:prop-5-1} for the given annulus. First assume
\(h<1/(8K)\). Put \(a=Kh\), \(b=2a\), and write
\(E(T,\tau)=\mathcal F(T,\tau)\) for the energy of Proposition~\ref{ms:prop-5-1}. This proposition supplies nonnegativity and smoothness on the open annulus \(a<|\tau|<4\), which contains the closed annulus \(b\le|\tau|\le3\). It also gives
\(\Delta_{T,\tau}E\le V(|\tau|)E\) on \(b<|\tau|<3\), with
\(V(s)=Cs^{-2}e^{-cs/h}\). For \ref{ms:lemma-6-1} the required
integral is uniformly bounded because
\[
 \int_b^3s\log(s/b)V(s)\,ds
 \le C\int_1^\infty \frac{\log t}{t}\,e^{-2cKt}\,dt .
\]
Also \(V\) is uniformly bounded on \([1/2,3/2]\). The bounds of
\ref{ms:prop-5-1} at the two circles hold uniformly on each
circle. Thus the circular mean \(H\) of \(E\) satisfies
\[
 H(0,2b)\le Ca^2\|f\|_{p_c}^{p_c},\qquad
 H(T,b)\ge ca^2\|U(T)f\|_{p_c}^{p_c}\quad(1\le T\le2).
\]
Use \ref{ms:lemma-6-1} at \(r=2b\), cancel \(a^2\), and take
\(p_c\)-th roots. This gives the claim because \(K\) is fixed and
\(\log(3/(2Kh))\lesssim\log(2/h)\).

removed by rescaling. When \(h\ge1/(8K)\) all contributing
frequencies are in the fixed ball \(|\xi|\le8KC_0\).

a constant times \(\|f\|_{p_c}\) by Hölder's inequality, and
\(e^{-iT|\xi|}\) has modulus one. Summing the resulting finitely
many pointwise bounds proves the estimate in this range as well.

levels.component_tex:
Let $n\ge2$, $d=n-1$, $X=(x,b)$ be an orthonormal spatial frame, and $u_{\rm w}=\sum_{\kappa,v}u_{\kappa,v}$ be a finite superposition of forward-wave modes. The sum ranges over an arbitrary finite set of distinct frequencies $\xi=(\xi_x,\xi_b)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R$ with $\xi_b+|\xi|>0$, relabelled by $(\kappa,v)$; each coefficient $c_{\kappa,v}\in\mathbb C$ is arbitrary. For each such frequency set
\[
\kappa=(\xi_b+|\xi|)/\sqrt2>0,\qquad v=\xi_x/\kappa,\qquad
u_{\kappa,v}=c_{\kappa,v}e^{\mathrm i(X\cdot\xi-T|\xi|)}.
\]
Use quaternionic units $\mathbf i,\mathbf j,\mathbf k$ with $\mathbf{ij}=\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf{ki}=\mathbf j$, and let $\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}=\mathbb R+\mathbf k\mathbb R$. Use null coordinates $\mathsf X=(t,x,s_0)$, with $t=(T+b)/\sqrt2$ and $s_0=(b-T)/\sqrt2$. Denote the corresponding complex auxiliary coordinates by $\omega=(Y,P,S_1)\in\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}\times\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}^d\times\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}$. For $Y\ne0$ set
\[
y=|Y|,\quad e=Y/y,\quad W=P/Y,\quad
\Phi=S_1+\frac{P\cdot P}{2Y},\quad
V^v=\bigl(1,(v+W)/2,-W\cdot v/2\bigr)^{\mathsf t}.
\]
Dots of complex vectors are bilinear. In the physical frame, the auxiliary coordinates are $(\tau,P,Z)$, with $Y=(\tau+Z)/\sqrt2$, $S_1=(Z-\tau)/\sqrt2$. For real $\alpha,\beta$ define $\iota_e(\alpha+\mathrm i\beta)=\alpha+e\mathbf i\beta$. Put
\[
m_{\kappa,v}=(\kappa/y)^{d/2}e^{-\kappa y|W-v|^2/2},\qquad
\chi=\sum_{\kappa,v} V^v\iota_e(\overline{u_{\kappa,v}})m_{\kappa,v},\qquad A^0=\chi\chi^* .
\]
Write $x_{\mu0}=\mathsf X_\mu$ and $\omega_\mu=x_{\mu1}+\mathbf kx_{\mu2}$ in the matching order $\mu=0,\ldots,n$. For a holomorphic scalar or vector function $F$ of $\omega$, write $\partial F$ for its complex Jacobian with columns $\partial_{\omega_\mu}F$, where $\partial_{\omega_\mu}=(\partial_{x_{\mu1}}-\mathbf k\partial_{x_{\mu2}})/2$. Both $\chi$ and $A^0$ are smooth, $A^0\ge0$, and
\[
(\partial\Phi)V^v=0,\qquad
(\partial W)V^v=\frac{v-W}{2Y},\qquad
(\partial\Phi)A^0=0 .
\]
Each real column of $(A^0)^\mathbb R$, with entries
\[
(A^0)^\mathbb R_{\mu\alpha,\nu\beta}=\operatorname{Re}(\bar e_\alpha A^0_{\mu\nu}e_\beta),
\qquad (e_0,e_1,e_2)=(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j),
\]
has zero divergence, meaning that for every column index $(\nu,\beta)$,
\[
 \sum_{\mu=0}^n\sum_{\alpha=0}^2
 \partial_{x_{\mu\alpha}}(A^0)^\mathbb R_{\mu\alpha,\nu\beta}=0.
\]
These conclusions hold in the physical coordinates by the orthogonal change on all three slots. In that frame
\[
V_T^v=(1+W\cdot v/2)/\sqrt2,\qquad A^0_{TT}=|\chi_T|^2.
\]
At a fixed auxiliary point let $\mathsf S_0,\mathsf S_1$ multiply each spatial mode of $u_{\rm w}$ by $b_0m_{\kappa,v},b_1m_{\kappa,v}$, where $b_0,b_1\in\mathbb R$ are defined by $V_T^v=b_0+\mathbf k b_1$. Then
\[
b_0=\frac{1+\operatorname{Re}(W)\cdot v/2}{\sqrt2},
\qquad
b_1=\frac{\operatorname{Im}_{\mathbf k}(W)\cdot v}{2\sqrt2},
\qquad A^0_{TT}=|\mathsf S_0u_{\rm w}|^2+|\mathsf S_1u_{\rm w}|^2.
\]

levels.title: The Euclidean wave current

levels.component_tex:
Let $n\ge2$, $d=n-1$, $0<h\le1$, and $0<c_0<C_0$. In any orthonormal frame $(x,b)$ on the covering space of $\mathbb T^n=\mathbb R^n/(100\mathbb Z^n)$, write $\xi=(\xi_x,\xi_b)$ and $\kappa=(\xi_b+|\xi|)/\sqrt2$. For frequencies with $\kappa>0$ put $v=\xi_x/\kappa$, and assume $c_0\le h|\xi|\le C_0$ and $|v|\le1/10$. For $y>0$ and $W\in\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}^d$ with $|W|\le1/10$, where $\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}=\mathbb R+\mathbf k\mathbb R$ and $\mathbf k^2=-1$, let
\[
 b_0=\frac{1+\operatorname{Re}(W)\cdot v/2}{\sqrt2},\qquad
 \Psi=\kappa y|W-v|^2/2,\qquad
 m_0=b_0(\kappa/y)^{d/2}e^{-\Psi}.
\]
Write $\mathsf S_0$ for the multiplier that multiplies the coefficient at $\xi$ by $m_0$. On these frequencies, $\kappa\asymp h^{-1}$, $b_0\asymp1$, and
\[
 m_0^{-1}=b_0^{-1}(y/\kappa)^{d/2}e^\Psi
     \asymp(hy)^{d/2}e^\Psi .
\]
In particular $h^d m_0\asymp1$ if $y\asymp h$.

If $f(X)=\sum_\xi c_\xi e^{\mathrm i X\cdot\xi}$ is a trigonometric polynomial on $\mathbb T^n$ supported on these frequencies, then the number of supported frequencies is $O(h^{-n})$ and $\sum_\xi|c_\xi|\lesssim h^{-n/2}\|f\|_2$. The norm uses ordinary torus volume. The estimates are uniform in the frame, with constants depending on $n,c_0,C_0$ and, for the two-sided bound when $y\asymp h$, the fixed comparison constants for $y/h$.

levels.component_tex:
For Hermitian quaternionic $m\times m$ matrices set $A:B=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(AB)$. Write $\det A$ for the Moore determinant, the product of the real eigenvalues counted with quaternionic multiplicity. It is a homogeneous polynomial of degree $m$. Its cofactor $C(A)$ is the Hermitian matrix determined by
\[
C(A):B=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\det(A+tB)\right|_{t=0}.
\]
It is polynomial of degree $m-1$, with $C(A)=(\det A)A^{-1}$ for $A>0$. For $A\ge0$ one has $C(A)\ge0$, and when $A$ is also singular, $C(A)$ kills the image of $A$. On positive definite matrices $\log\det$ is concave and increasing in the matrix order.

For every Hermitian $A$, unit vector $v\in\mathbb H^m$ and real $t$,
\[
v^*C(A)v=\det(A|_{v^\perp}),\qquad
\det(A+tvv^*)=\det A+t\,v^*C(A)v,
\]
where $A|_{v^\perp}$ is compression to the quaternionic orthogonal complement and the determinant in dimension zero is one. For a Hermitian $M=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\ell&c^*\\c&D\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with $D>0$, put $\sigma=\ell-c^*D^{-1}c$ and let $v_0$ be the first coordinate vector. Then
\[
\det M=(\det D)\sigma,\qquad M-\sigma v_0v_0^*\ge0.
\]

levels.component_tex:
Let $k=3$ or $4$, use $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j,\mathbf k)$, and write $z_a=\sum_{\alpha=0}^{k-1}e_\alpha z_{a\alpha}$ for $1\le a\le m$. For a real $C^2$ function $u$, define
\[
G_a(u)=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha\partial_{a\alpha}u,\qquad
H_{ab}(u)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}e_\alpha\bar e_\beta\,
       \partial_{a\alpha}\partial_{b\beta}u,\qquad
\partial_{a\alpha}=\partial/\partial z_{a\alpha}.
\]
Then $H(u)$ is Hermitian and $\operatorname{tr}H(u)=\Delta u$. The map from the real Hessian to $H(u)$ sends the real rank-one matrix $\xi\xi^{\mathsf t}$ to $gg^*$, where $g_a=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha\xi_{a\alpha}$, and sends nonnegative real matrices to nonnegative quaternionic matrices. For real $C^2$ functions $u,v$,
\[
H(uv)=uH(v)+vH(u)+G(u)G(v)^*+G(v)G(u)^* .
\]
In four slots $H$ is covariant under quaternionic unitary changes of coordinates, and in three slots it is covariant under real orthogonal changes of the index $a$ applied in all slots. If $u$ depends only on $P\in\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}^m$ in $z_a=x_a+P_a\mathbf i$ (and is independent of the fourth slot if present), write $P_a=p_a+\mathbf k q_a$ and use
\[
\partial_{P_a}=\tfrac12(\partial_{p_a}-\mathbf k\partial_{q_a}),\qquad
\partial_{\bar P_a}=\tfrac12(\partial_{p_a}+\mathbf k\partial_{q_a}).
\]
With this convention,
\[
G_a(u)=2(\partial_{\bar P_a}u)\mathbf i,\qquad
H_{ab}(u)=4\partial_{\bar P_a}\partial_{P_b}u .
\]

levels.statement:
Let $k=3$ or $4$, use $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j,\mathbf k)$, and write $z_a=\sum_{\alpha=0}^{k-1}e_\alpha z_{a\alpha}$ for $1\le a\le m$. For a real $C^2$ function $u$, define
\[
G_a(u)=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha\partial_{a\alpha}u,\qquad
H_{ab}(u)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}e_\alpha\bar e_\beta\,
       \partial_{a\alpha}\partial_{b\beta}u,\qquad
\partial_{a\alpha}=\partial/\partial z_{a\alpha}.
\]
Then $H(u)$ is Hermitian and $\operatorname{tr}H(u)=\Delta u$. The map from the real Hessian to $H(u)$ sends the real rank-one matrix $\xi\xi^{\mathsf t}$ to $gg^*$, where $g_a=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha\xi_{a\alpha}$, and sends nonnegative real matrices to nonnegative quaternionic matrices. For real $C^2$ functions $u,v$,
\[
H(uv)=uH(v)+vH(u)+G(u)G(v)^*+G(v)G(u)^* .
\]
In four slots $H$ is covariant under quaternionic unitary changes of coordinates, and in three slots it is covariant under real orthogonal changes of the index $a$ applied in all slots. If $u$ depends only on $P\in\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}^m$ in $z_a=x_a+P_a\mathbf i$ (and is independent of the fourth slot if present), write $P_a=p_a+\mathbf k q_a$ and use
\[
\partial_{P_a}=\tfrac12(\partial_{p_a}-\mathbf k\partial_{q_a}),\qquad
\partial_{\bar P_a}=\tfrac12(\partial_{p_a}+\mathbf k\partial_{q_a}).
\]
With this convention,
\[

H_{ab}(u)=4\partial_{\bar P_a}\partial_{P_b}u .

levels.title: Quaternionic Hessian calculus

levels.component_tex:
Let $n\ge2$, $d=n-1$, $w_0=1/10$, $a>0$, $s=|\tau|$, and $z=(T,\tau)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}$ with $a<s<4$. At fixed $z$, write $X\in\mathbb R^n/(100\mathbb Z^n)$ and $(P,Z)\in\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}^d\times\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}$. On $Y\ne0$ define
\[
 Y=(\tau+Z)/\sqrt 2,\qquad W=P/Y,\qquad
 \Phi=(Z-\tau)/\sqrt 2+(P\cdot P)/(2Y),\qquad Q=\Phi/a .
\]
Here the dot denotes the complex bilinear product and the norm is Euclidean. Let $\Omega_z$ be the fiber $r<0$ in this open set, where $r=|W|^2/w_0^2+100|Q|^2-1$, and put
$\Omega=\{(z,X,P,Z):a<s<4,\ (X,P,Z)\in\Omega_z\}$. For the full operators use $n+1$ real triples $x_{j0}+x_{j1}\mathbf i+x_{j2}\mathbf j$ with real slots $(T,X)$ and auxiliary slots given by $(\tau,P,Z)\mathbf i$, in matching index order. Thus if an auxiliary coordinate is $p+\mathbf kq$, its slots are $(x_{j1},x_{j2})=(p,q)$. Write $(e_0,e_1,e_2)=(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j)$, $\partial_{j\alpha}=\partial/\partial x_{j\alpha}$, and set
\[
G_j(v)=\sum_{\alpha=0}^2 e_\alpha\partial_{j\alpha}v,\qquad
H_{jk}(v)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^2 e_\alpha\bar e_\beta\partial_{j\alpha}\partial_{k\beta}v.
\]
The spatial operators $G_{\rm fib},H_{\rm fib}$ use only the $n$ indices belonging to $(X,P,Z)$ at fixed $(T,\tau)$. Write $\mathrm d\zeta=\mathrm dX\,\mathrm dP\,\mathrm dZ$ for ordinary fiber volume.

The fiber chart $(P,Z)\mapsto(W,Q)$ is a biholomorphism to the ellipsoid $|W|^2/w_0^2+100|Q|^2<1$ and extends to neighborhoods of the closures. Its inverse is
\[
 Y=\frac{\sqrt 2\,\tau+aQ}{1+W\cdot W/2},\qquad P=WY,\qquad Z=\sqrt 2\,Y-\tau .
\]
On the closed fibers, uniformly for $a<s<4$, one has $|Y|\asymp s$ and
\begin{align*}
 H_{\rm fib}(r)&\ge c s^{-2}I,
 &G_{\rm fib}(r)G_{\rm fib}(r)^*&\le H_{\rm fib}(r),\\
 \mathrm dP\,\mathrm dZ&\asymp a^2s^{2d}\,\mathrm dW\,\mathrm dQ,
 &\det H_{\rm fib}(r)&\asymp a^{-2}s^{-2d}.
\end{align*}
The full $H(r)$ is positive semidefinite with a one-dimensional quaternionic kernel contained in $G(r)^\perp\cap\ker H(|\Phi|^2)$. The spatial $H_{\rm fib}(|\Phi|^2)$ has rank one and nonzero eigenvalue comparable to one. The full gradient satisfies $|G(|W|^2)|\lesssim s^{-1}$.

levels.title: Fiber geometry

levels.component_tex:
Let $m\ge1$, let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a full lattice, and let $V\subset\mathbb R^{2m}$ be a bounded smooth domain. Write $\Omega=(\mathbb R^m/\Lambda)\times V$. Write $x_{a0}$ for the periodic coordinates and group the remaining coordinates of $V$ as $(x_{a1},x_{a2})_{a=1}^m$ in the $\mathbf i,\mathbf j$ slots. Set $(e_0,e_1,e_2)=(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j)$ and $\partial_{a\alpha}=\partial/\partial x_{a\alpha}$. For a real function $v$, the three-slot Hessian is
\[
H_{ab}(v)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^2e_\alpha\bar e_\beta\,\partial_{a\alpha}\partial_{b\beta}v .
\]
The determinant is the Moore determinant. Let $r\in C^\infty(\overline V)$ be a defining function, negative in $V$, with $\mathrm dr\ne0$ on $\partial V$ and $H(r)>0$ on $\overline\Omega$. Suppose $B_0,g\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)$ are real and satisfy
\[
 H(B_0)\ge0,\qquad g>\det H(B_0)\quad\text{on }\overline\Omega .
\]
Then there is a unique smooth solution up to the boundary of
\[
 \det H(B_0+u)=g,\qquad H(B_0+u)>0,\qquad u|_{\partial\Omega}=0.
\]
There are constants $b\ge b'>0$ such that $br\le u\le b'r$. For smooth finite-dimensional families of such domains and data, the barrier constants may be chosen locally uniformly, and the solutions depend smoothly on the parameters up to the boundary after a smooth local identification of domains.

The comparison principle also holds on subdomains with the same three-slot operator. If two smooth real potentials $\psi_i$ have positive definite Hessians up to the boundary, $\det H(\psi_1)\ge\det H(\psi_2)$ in the subdomain and $\psi_1\le\psi_2$ on its boundary, then $\psi_1\le\psi_2$ throughout.

levels.title: Periodic Dirichlet problem

levels.component_tex:
Use the three-slot fiber with $Y=(\tau+Z)/\sqrt 2$, $W=P/Y$, $\Phi=(Z-\tau)/\sqrt 2+(P\cdot P)/(2Y)$, $Q=\Phi/a$, and $r=|W|^2/w_0^2+100|Q|^2-1$, where $w_0=1/10$, $a=Kh$, $K\ge1$, $d=n-1$, and $n\ge2$. Let $z=(T,\tau)$, $s=|\tau|$, $a<s<4$, and take $\Omega_z=\{r<0\}$ in the variables $(X,P,Z)$ with $X$ on the fixed spatial torus and $Y\ne0$. Write $x_{j0}$ for the real coordinates $(T,X)$ and $x_{j1}+\mathbf kx_{j2}$ for the corresponding auxiliary coordinates $(\tau,P,Z)$. Let $(e_0,e_1,e_2)=(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j)$, with $\mathbf k\mathbf i=\mathbf j$, and write $\partial_{j\alpha}=\partial/\partial x_{j\alpha}$. Set
\[
 G_j(w)=\sum_{\alpha=0}^2 e_\alpha\partial_{j\alpha}w,\qquad
 H_{jk}(w)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^2 e_\alpha\bar e_\beta\partial_{j\alpha}\partial_{k\beta}w .
\]
A subscript $\mathrm{fib}$ restricts to spatial indices. Use the Moore determinant and its cofactor $C$, characterized by
$\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(C(D)M)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\det(D+tM)\right|_{t=0}$
for Hermitian $M$.

Let $f$ be a trigonometric polynomial on this torus with $\|f\|_2=1$, frequencies in a fixed annulus $c_0\le h|\xi|\le C_0$ with $0<c_0<C_0$. In the chosen frame $X=(x,b)$, assume the supported frequencies have $\kappa=(\xi_b+|\xi|)/\sqrt2>0$ and $|v|\le\gamma<w_0/4$, where $v=\xi_x/\kappa$. Set $y=|Y|$, $e=Y/y$, and $\iota_e(\alpha+\mathrm i\beta)=\alpha+e\mathbf i\beta$ for real $\alpha,\beta$. To obtain the wave current, form the following column in null coordinates $t=(T+b)/\sqrt2$, $s_0=(b-T)/\sqrt2$:
\[
 \chi=\sum_{\xi}
 \begin{pmatrix}1\\(v+W)/2\\-W\cdot v/2\end{pmatrix}
 \iota_e\!\bigl(\overline{\widehat f(\xi)e^{\mathrm i(X\cdot\xi-T|\xi|)}}\bigr)
 (\kappa/y)^{d/2}e^{-\kappa y|W-v|^2/2}.
\]
Use the orthogonal change of index from $(t,x,s_0)$ to $(T,x,b)$ to express $\chi$ in physical coordinates and set $A^0=\chi\chi^*$ there. For $\ell>0$ let $J_\ell$ be the periodization of the probability kernel $c_n\ell^{-n}(1+|X/\ell|^2)^{-n-2}$, with $c_n$ normalizing the integral. Fix a smooth $0\le g\le1$ on $\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}$ equal to one on $|Q|\le1/100$ and zero on $|Q|\ge1/20$. Define
\[
 A_{\rm w}=g(Q)(J_h*_X A^0),\qquad A=A_{\rm w}+h^{50n}C(H(r)),\qquad
 \mu=A_{TT},\qquad B_0=\lambda|\Phi|^2,\qquad\lambda=h^{-30n}.
\]
Here $*_X$ denotes convolution in the real periodic variables only. Put $B=H(B_0)$ and $B_{\rm fib}=H_{\rm fib}(B_0)$.

For sufficiently small $h>0$ with $4a\le1$, take the zero-boundary Dirichlet solution $u$ with $D_u>0$ and $\det D_u=\lambda\mu$, where $D_v=H_{\rm fib}(B_0+v)$. Write $\mathrm d\zeta=\mathrm dX\,\mathrm dP\,\mathrm dZ$,
\[
 X_0(z)=\int_{\Omega_z}(-u)\mu\,\mathrm d\zeta,\qquad
 E_z(v)=\lambda^{-1}\int_{\Omega_z}v\int_0^1\det D_{\theta v}\,\mathrm d\theta\,\mathrm d\zeta,\qquad
 \mathcal F(z)=E_z(u)+X_0(z).
\]
If $H(B_0+u)=\begin{pmatrix}\ell&c^*\\c&D_u\end{pmatrix}$, put
$\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}c^*D_u^{-1}c&c^*\\c&D_u\end{pmatrix}$.
Let $\rho$ denote the smooth boundary value of $u/r$. Then $\mathcal F$ is smooth for $a<|\tau|<4$, $\Sigma\ge0$, and
\[
 \Delta_z\mathcal F(z)+\int_{\Omega_z} A:\Sigma\,\mathrm d\zeta
 =\int \rho\, G(r)^*A_{\rm w}G(r)\,\delta(r)\,\mathrm d\zeta .
\]
Here $A:\Sigma=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(A\Sigma)$, $\Delta_z$ is the Laplacian in the three real coordinates of $z$, $G(r)$ is the full gradient, and $\delta(r)\,\mathrm d\zeta=\mathrm dS_{\rm fib}/|\nabla_{\rm fib}r|$ on the fixed fiber wall. In particular the right-hand side is an upper bound on $\Delta_z\mathcal F$.

Here $*_X$ denotes convolution in the real periodic variables only. Put $B=H(B_0)$ and $B_{\rm fib}=H_{\rm fib}(B_0)$.

For sufficiently small $h>0$ with $4a\le1$, take the zero-boundary Dirichlet solution $u$ with $D_u>0$ and $\det D_u=\lambda\mu$, where $D_v=H_{\rm fib}(B_0+v)$. Write $\mathrm d\zeta=\mathrm dX\,\mathrm dP\,\mathrm dZ$,
\[
 X_0(z)=\int_{\Omega_z}(-u)\mu\,\mathrm d\zeta,\qquad
 E_z(v)=\lambda^{-1}\int_{\Omega_z}v\int_0^1\det D_{\theta v}\,\mathrm d\theta\,\mathrm d\zeta,\qquad
 \mathcal F(z)=E_z(u)+X_0(z).
\]
If $H(B_0+u)=\begin{pmatrix}\ell&c^*\\c&D_u\end{pmatrix}$, put
$\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}c^*D_u^{-1}c&c^*\\c&D_u\end{pmatrix}$.
Let $\rho$ denote the smooth boundary value of $u/r$. Then $\mathcal F$ is smooth for $a<|\tau|<4$, $\Sigma\ge0$, and
\[
 \Delta_z\mathcal F(z)+\int_{\Omega_z} A:\Sigma\,\mathrm d\zeta
 =\int \rho\, G(r)^*A_{\rm w}G(r)\,\delta(r)\,\mathrm d\zeta .
\]
Here $A:\Sigma=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(A\Sigma)$, $\Delta_z$ is the Laplacian in the three real coordinates of $z$, $G(r)$ is the full gradient, and $\delta(r)\,\mathrm d\zeta=\mathrm dS_{\rm fib}/|\nabla_{\rm fib}r|$ on the fixed fiber wall. levels.text:
Use the three-slot fiber with $Y=(\tau+Z)/\sqrt 2$, $W=P/Y$, $\Phi=(Z-\tau)/\sqrt 2+(P\cdot P)/(2Y)$, $Q=\Phi/a$, and $r=|W|^2/w_0^2+100|Q|^2-1$, where $w_0=1/10$, $a=Kh$, $K\ge1$, $d=n-1$, and $n\ge2$. Let $z=(T,\tau)$, $s=|\tau|$, $a<s<4$, and take $\Omega_z=\{r<0\}$ in the variables $(X,P,Z)$ with $X$ on the fixed spatial torus and $Y\ne0$. Write $x_{j0}$ for the real coordinates $(T,X)$ and $x_{j1}+\mathbf kx_{j2}$ for the corresponding auxiliary coordinates $(\tau,P,Z)$. Let $(e_0,e_1,e_2)=(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j)$, with $\mathbf k\mathbf i=\mathbf j$, and write $\partial_{j\alpha}=\partial/\partial x_{j\alpha}$. Set
\[
 G_j(w)=\sum_{\alpha=0}^2 e_\alpha\partial_{j\alpha}w,\qquad
 H_{jk}(w)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^2 e_\alpha\bar e_\beta\partial_{j\alpha}\partial_{k\beta}w .
\]
A subscript $\mathrm{fib}$ restricts to spatial indices. Use the Moore determinant and its cofactor $C$, characterized by
$\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(C(D)M)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\det(D+tM)\right|_{t=0}$
for Hermitian $M$.

Let $f$ be a trigonometric polynomial on this torus with $\|f\|_2=1$, frequencies in a fixed annulus $c_0\le h|\xi|\le C_0$ with $0<c_0<C_0$. In the chosen frame $X=(x,b)$, assume the supported frequencies have $\kappa=(\xi_b+|\xi|)/\sqrt2>0$ and $|v|\le\gamma<w_0/4$, where $v=\xi_x/\kappa$. Set $y=|Y|$, $e=Y/y$, and $\iota_e(\alpha+\mathrm i\beta)=\alpha+e\mathbf i\beta$ for real $\alpha,\beta$. To obtain the wave current, form the following column in null coordinates $t=(T+b)/\sqrt2$, $s_0=(b-T)/\sqrt2$:
\[
 \chi=\sum_{\xi}
 \begin{pmatrix}1\\(v+W)/2\\-W\cdot v/2\end{pmatrix}
 \iota_e\!\bigl(\overline{\widehat f(\xi)e^{\mathrm i(X\cdot\xi-T|\xi|)}}\bigr)
 (\kappa/y)^{d/2}e^{-\kappa y|W-v|^2/2}.
\]
Use the orthogonal change of index from $(t,x,s_0)$ to $(T,x,b)$ to express $\chi$ in physical coordinates and set $A^0=\chi\chi^*$ there. For $\ell>0$ let $J_\ell$ be the periodization of the probability kernel $c_n\ell^{-n}(1+|X/\ell|^2)^{-n-2}$, with $c_n$ normalizing the integral. Fix a smooth $0\le g\le1$ on $\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}$ equal to one on $|Q|\le1/100$ and zero on $|Q|\ge1/20$. Define
\[
 A_{\rm w}=g(Q)(J_h*_X A^0),\qquad A=A_{\rm w}+h^{50n}C(H(r)),\qquad
 \mu=A_{TT},\qquad B_0=\lambda|\Phi|^2,\qquad\lambda=h^{-30n}.
\]
Here $*_X$ denotes convolution in the real periodic variables only. Put $B=H(B_0)$ and $B_{\rm fib}=H_{\rm fib}(B_0)$.

For sufficiently small $h>0$ with $4a\le1$, take the zero-boundary Dirichlet solution $u$ with $D_u>0$ and $\det D_u=\lambda\mu$, where $D_v=H_{\rm fib}(B_0+v)$. Write $\mathrm d\zeta=\mathrm dX\,\mathrm dP\,\mathrm dZ$,
\[
 X_0(z)=\int_{\Omega_z}(-u)\mu\,\mathrm d\zeta,\qquad
 E_z(v)=\lambda^{-1}\int_{\Omega_z}v\int_0^1\det D_{\theta v}\,\mathrm d\theta\,\mathrm d\zeta,\qquad
 \mathcal F(z)=E_z(u)+X_0(z).
\]
If $H(B_0+u)=\begin{pmatrix}\ell&c^*\\c&D_u\end{pmatrix}$, put
$\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}c^*D_u^{-1}c&c^*\\c&D_u\end{pmatrix}$.
Let $\rho$ denote the smooth boundary value of $u/r$. Then $\mathcal F$ is smooth for $a<|\tau|<4$, $\Sigma\ge0$, and
\[
 \Delta_z\mathcal F(z)+\int_{\Omega_z} A:\Sigma\,\mathrm d\zeta
 =\int \rho\, G(r)^*A_{\rm w}G(r)\,\delta(r)\,\mathrm d\zeta .
\]
Here $A:\Sigma=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(A\Sigma)$, $\Delta_z$ is the Laplacian in the three real coordinates of $z$, $G(r)$ is the full gradient, and $\delta(r)\,\mathrm d\zeta=\mathrm dS_{\rm fib}/|\nabla_{\rm fib}r|$ on the fixed fiber wall. In particular the right-hand side is an upper bound on $\Delta_z\mathcal F$.

Let $\mathbb H$ be the real associative algebra with basis $(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j,\mathbf k)$, unit $1$, and multiplication determined by
$\mathbf i^2=\mathbf j^2=\mathbf k^2=-1$, $\mathbf i\mathbf j=\mathbf k$, $\mathbf j\mathbf k=\mathbf i$, and $\mathbf k\mathbf i=\mathbf j$, with the opposite products having the opposite signs. Quaternionic conjugation is
$\overline{q_0+q_1\mathbf i+q_2\mathbf j+q_3\mathbf k}=q_0-q_1\mathbf i-q_2\mathbf j-q_3\mathbf k$.
Write $\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}=\{x+\mathbf k y:x,y\in\mathbb R\}$ for the complex subalgebra with the inherited multiplication and conjugation. We use quaternionic columns with scalars acting on the right, and $A^*$ denotes quaternionic conjugate transpose.

Fix an integer $n\ge2$, a real parameter $a>0$, and $z=(T,\tau)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}$ with $a<|\tau|<4$. Let $\Omega_z=(\mathbb R^n/(100\mathbb Z^n))\times V_z$, where $V_z$ is the open set of $(P,Z)\in\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}^{n-1}\times\mathbb C_{\mathbf k}$ for which
\[
 Y=(\tau+Z)/\sqrt2\ne0,\qquad
 100\left|P/Y\right|^2+100\left|\frac{(Z-\tau)/\sqrt2+P\cdot P/(2Y)}{a}\right|^2<1,
\]
with $P\cdot P$ using the bilinear dot product. Write $x_{j0}$ for the spatial torus coordinates and $x_{j1}+\mathbf k x_{j2}$ for the components of $(P,Z)$ in matching order. With $(e_0,e_1,e_2)=(1,\mathbf i,\mathbf j)$ and $\partial_{j\alpha}=\partial/\partial x_{j\alpha}$, put
\[
G_{{\rm fib},j}(v)=\sum_{\alpha=0}^2e_\alpha\partial_{j\alpha}v,\qquad
H_{{\rm fib},jk}(v)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^2 e_\alpha\bar e_\beta
      \partial_{j\alpha}\partial_{k\beta}v .
\]
Use the Moore determinant on Hermitian quaternionic matrices. Its cofactor is defined by
$\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(C(D)B)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\det(D+tB)\right|_{t=0}$
for Hermitian $B$. Let $B_0\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega_z;\mathbb R)$ have positive semidefinite spatial quaternionic Hessian $B_{\rm fib}=H_{\rm fib}(B_0)$ of rank one. Let $\lambda>0$ be a constant and $\mu:\overline\Omega_z\to(0,\infty)$ the smooth Dirichlet density. Let $u\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega_z;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $u\le0$, $u|_{\partial\Omega_z}=0$, $D_u>0$ in $\Omega_z$, and $\det D_u=\lambda\mu$, where $D_v=H_{\rm fib}(B_0+v)$. Set
\[
 \mathcal F=\lambda^{-1}\int_{\Omega_z}u\int_0^1\det D_{\theta u}\,\mathrm d\theta\,\mathrm d\zeta
  -\int_{\Omega_z}u\mu\,\mathrm d\zeta,
 \qquad X_0=\int_{\Omega_z}(-u)\mu\,\mathrm d\zeta.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal F=\frac{n-1}{n+1}X_0+\frac{1}{\lambda n(n+1)}
 \int_{\Omega_z} G_{\rm fib}(u)^* C(D_u)G_{\rm fib}(u)\,\mathrm d\zeta,
 \qquad
 \frac{n-1}{n+1}X_0\le\mathcal F\le\frac n{n+1}X_0.
\]
Here $\mathrm d\zeta=\mathrm dX\,\mathrm dP\,\mathrm dZ$ is ordinary fiber volume.
